disclaimer: This report is for educational and wellness purposes only. It is not a medical diagnosis and does not replace advice from a qualified healthcare professional. HbA1c results should be confirmed by your doctor. Do not start, stop or change any medication without medical advice.

status.label: In the prediabetes range
status.explanation: Your HbA1c is between 5.7% and 6.4%, the range used for prediabetes. This is a common and often reversible stage where lifestyle changes make the biggest difference.

summary: Your HbA1c of 6.1% falls in the prediabetes range, which means your blood sugar is higher than typical but not yet in the diabetes range. Your main risk factors are a BMI in the obese range, low physical activity, a family history of diabetes, and being over 45. The most valuable next steps are keeping track of your HbA1c and fasting blood sugar over time, becoming more physically active in a gradual way, and following the calorie target of 1500 calories to support a healthier weight. These changes can meaningfully lower your risk of moving into the diabetes range.

foods_to_eat: Whole grains like brown rice, millets and whole wheat
Pulses and legumes such as moong, chana and rajma
Non-starchy vegetables like spinach, lauki, beans and cauliflower
Lean proteins like fish, eggs and skinless chicken
Nuts and seeds in small portions
Low-fat dairy like curd and buttermilk
Seasonal low-glycaemic fruits like guava and apple
foods_to_avoid: Sugary drinks like soda and packaged juices
Refined flour products like white bread and maida snacks
Deep-fried foods like samosas and pakoras
Sweets and desserts high in sugar
plan.portion_guidance: Fill half your plate with vegetables, a quarter with whole grains, and a quarter with protein at lunch and dinner. Use a katori for lentils and curries, and keep rice or roti portions modest in size.
plan.hydration: Aim for about 8 to 10 glasses of water through the day. Limit sugary drinks and choose buttermilk or plain water instead.
based_on: obese BMI category: focus on portion control and fibre-rich foods

exercise: Start with 10-15 minutes of brisk walking or light cycling most days, and gradually build up over several weeks.
Aim for at least 150 minutes a week of moderate activity, such as brisk walking, cycling, or swimming, spread across the week.
Add simple muscle-strengthening exercises, like bodyweight squats, wall push-ups, or resistance band work, on 2 non-consecutive days.
Break up long periods of sitting by standing or moving for a few minutes every hour.
lifestyle.walking_goal: Begin with 15-20 minutes of walking a day, 5 days a week, and build up gradually to at least 30 minutes a day, 5-6 days a week.
lifestyle.weight_management: Your BMI is in the obese range, which means working toward gradual, steady weight loss can help lower your long-term health risks. Focus on building sustainable habits like regular movement, portion awareness, and balanced meals rather than quick fixes. Aim for slow, steady progress, such as losing a small percentage of body weight over several months, which can meaningfully improve blood sugar and overall health.
lifestyle.sleep: Aim for 7-9 hours of sleep each night. Try to keep a consistent bedtime and wake time, even on weekends. Avoid screens and caffeine close to bedtime, and create a cool, dark, quiet sleeping environment to support better rest.
stress: Practice deep breathing exercises, such as inhaling for 4 counts, holding for 4, and exhaling for 4, for a few minutes daily.
Try progressive muscle relaxation or a short daily mindfulness or meditation practice using a free app or guided audio.
Make time for enjoyable activities or hobbies, and connect regularly with friends or family for emotional support.
behaviour_change: Since you drink occasionally, consider keeping track of how much and how often to ensure it stays light and infrequent, and have alcohol-free days each week.
Set small, specific goals, like a daily walk or one extra vegetable serving, and track your progress to build momentum over time.
Consider connecting with a support group, health coach, or community program focused on diabetes prevention, since these can improve long-term success.
Involve family members in healthy meal planning and activity, which can make changes easier to sustain, especially given your family history of diabetes.

monitoring.name: HbA1c
monitoring.why: Catches progression from prediabetes to diabetes early.

monitoring.name: Fasting blood sugar
monitoring.why: Shows your blood glucose after an overnight fast and complements HbA1c.
monitoring.frequency: Alongside your HbA1c test, or as your doctor advises

monitoring.name: Blood pressure
monitoring.why: High blood pressure multiplies the heart and kidney risks of high blood glucose.
monitoring.frequency: At every doctor visit; at home regularly if you have high blood pressure

preventive_actions: Aim for short daily walks or other light movement to reduce sedentary time
Work toward the 1500 calorie target with balanced, consistent meals rather than skipping meals
Schedule regular checks of fasting blood sugar and blood pressure as suggested in your monitoring list
Include more vegetables, whole grains, and lean proteins in your usual Indian non-vegetarian meals
Track your weight periodically since BMI is currently in the obese range
Limit alcohol to occasional, light amounts to support stable blood sugar

hba1c_caveat: HbA1c can be less accurate if you have anaemia, kidney disease, a recent blood transfusion or certain haemoglobin variants.
